title: observability: token-level KV cache metrics + cost/latency dashboard and alert tuning
author: Avery Park
release_notes: Add token-level KV cache metrics and dashboards; tune alerts to reduce noise and align on cost/latency SLOs; no breaking changes.
description:
Context & motivation:
We continue to see customer-facing incidents where sudden KV cache pressure causes token-level cost and tail latency regressions for low-latency routes. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics (hits, misses, evictions, cache_age_histogram), integrates them with existing token-level cost/latency dashboards, and adjusts alert thresholds to reduce noise while catching true regressions.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add new metrics emitted from the serving runtime: redwood.kv.token_cache_hits, redwood.kv.token_cache_misses, redwood.kv.token_cache_evictions, redwood.kv.token_cache_age_seconds (histogram).
- Wire metrics through the tracing/span enrichment so traces include kv cache hit/miss metadata for sampled requests.
- Dashboard: update Token Cost & Latency dashboard to include KV cache panels and token-level breakdowns by model/route/tier.
- Alerts: tune existing token tail-latency alert and add a correlated alert for token-level KV miss rate > 5% sustained over 3m with cost increase delta > 15% over baseline.
- Tests & docs: unit tests for emitter, end-to-end integration test with local metrics server, and docs note for operators.

Review conversation (selected):
Priya Singh (reviewer): "Nice work — the metric names look consistent, but can we avoid adding high-cardinality tags on the emitter? I noticed model_version is attached to every metric."
Avery Park (author): "Good catch — I removed model_version from the metric labels and instead added it as trace/span attribute. Updated the emitter to use model_id and route_id only (low-cardinality)."

Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Alert looks promising but the 15% cost delta might be noisy for small routes. Can we make the rule scoped to routes with >1000 tokens/min?"
Avery Park: "Agreed — changed alert to only evaluate for routes with token_rate >= 1000. Added note in runbook about manual evaluation for low-volume routes."

Diego Alvarez (SRE): "Can you add an onboarding note for Dedicated customers who run Private (VPC) so they know how to map the metrics to their local exporters?"
Avery Park: "Added a section in docs/runbooks/kv-cache-incident.md and examples/observability/quickstart.md describing exporter mapping and Grafana import steps."

CI summary:

- integration-tests: fail (metrics integration test failed in first run due to timing race).
- lint: pass
Actions taken: fixed a race in metrics_server_test.go by adding a short backoff and a readiness check; re-ran CI; all checks pass.

Operational notes and rollout plan:
- Dashboard deployed to staging and validated with simulated KV miss traffic (script in tests/).
- Alerts deployed to staging alertmanager on 2025-11-18 for 48h observation window. After no regressions and tuned thresholds, promoted to prod on 2025-11-20.
- Rollout policy: monitor for increased alert noise for 72h; SRE to rollback alert threshold if noise > 5 alerts/hour for last 3h.

Why this matters:
- Token-level KV miss spikes are a clear leading indicator of token-level cost increases and tail-latency regressions; surfacing them and correlating in dashboards/traces lets teams diagnose and mitigate quickly without touching model configs.

Merge outcome:
- Squash-merged on 2025-11-20 after approvals from Priya, Liam, and Diego and green CI. Merge commit: a9f3d2b4c6e8f1b0d9e7c1234567890abcde1234.

Notes for follow-ups:
- Consider adding sampling adjustments to traces to ensure kv-miss events are captured more reliably for low-volume routes.
- Add a synthetic canary that exercises KV-heavy paths to provide continuous validation of thresholds.
